class.archer.lore:
Strikes true,
slips like a shadow.
class.archer.name: Archer
class.healer.name: Healer
class.mage.name: Mage
class.warrior.lore:
Iron fists,
a heart of steel.
class.warrior.name: Warrior
dlg.aldric.1: Hero... I heard you returned, but did not believe it until now.
dlg.aldric.10: The door opens only to a crystal-bearer; otherwise it is a wall.
dlg.aldric.11: Going there, returning is hard. Do not go unprepared.
dlg.aldric.12: Be swift, but do not hurry. They are not the same thing.
dlg.aldric.13: The Earth Crystal... do you feel the weight of what you hold?
dlg.aldric.14: That stone sat in a golem's chest for a hundred years.
dlg.aldric.15: The next lies on the Desert Road — not under the sand, but with those who live upon it.
dlg.aldric.16: Find the Oracle Nyx. She volunteers nothing; ask and she answers.
dlg.aldric.17: Ask well. She answers a wrong question truly, which helps no one.
dlg.aldric.19: Ah, young hero. You came at last. I have been waiting.
dlg.aldric.2: Malachar's seal is closed again. This time for good.
dlg.aldric.20: You will have heard my name: Aldric. Oldest man here, and the least useful.
dlg.aldric.21: A century ago our forebears sealed Malachar with four crystals.
dlg.aldric.22: The seal weakens. Night birds fell silent, waters darkened, beasts turned savage.
dlg.aldric.23: The four Sacred Crystals must be gathered again. My legs will not carry me.
dlg.aldric.24: Begin with the Dark Forest to the east. Sir Roland went there and never came back.
dlg.aldric.3: For the first time in three days the village slept without lamps.
dlg.aldric.4: The kingdom owes you. Whether we live to repay it, I cannot say.
dlg.aldric.5: Know this, though: your name will not be forgotten here.
dlg.aldric.6: Sit a while. Let us have tea and speak of something other than war.
dlg.aldric.7: The Water Crystal! So you went to the bottom of the Ice Cave.
dlg.aldric.8: Two of the four are ours. The seal is half restored.
dlg.aldric.9: The portal to the Shadow Castle lies in the cave's south-west corner.
dlg.avci.1: I carve my own bows and twist my own strings.
dlg.avci.10: A hunter who knows that lives long. Most die not knowing.
dlg.avci.11: My token is on the stall. Cheap, for you — you earned it.
dlg.avci.12: Come hunting with me one day. Talk comes easier in the woods.
dlg.avci.2: Something changed in the woods: wolves move in packs now.
dlg.avci.3: They used to hunt alone. Now they wait for one another.
dlg.avci.4: If you hunt, buy a good bow. A cheap one fails halfway.
dlg.avci.5: A string slackens in damp and snaps in cold. Mind both.
dlg.avci.6: I know nothing of close fighting. Whatever your trade, a bow serves.
dlg.avci.7: Three wolves? So you broke the pack.
dlg.avci.8: A lone wolf is timid; it thinks twice before closing in.
dlg.avci.9: In a pack they are another animal. The same wolf, a different beast.
dlg.ciftci.1: My field lies outside the village, on the eastern slope.
dlg.ciftci.10: I kept the seed for spring. If we see another spring.
dlg.ciftci.11: Buy what you like — I won't say free, but... thank you all the same.
dlg.ciftci.12: And take this. Don't pay; I'll just say I charged you.
dlg.ciftci.2: The boars are wild this year; they tear the crop out by the root.
dlg.ciftci.3: I brought what seed I had left to market, at least to sell it.
dlg.ciftci.4: That farm tool is good iron; it will strengthen your arm.
dlg.ciftci.5: This is my first time at market. I scarcely know how to set a stall.
dlg.ciftci.6: Better than sitting at home waiting. Waiting grows no crop.
dlg.ciftci.7: Was it you who scattered the boars? My field stood whole this morning.
dlg.ciftci.8: I may bring in a harvest this year, for once.
dlg.ciftci.9: I'll send word to Torben as well. He was worse off than I.
dlg.farmer.1: Welcome! I am Torben. Owner of that field, enemy of those boars.
dlg.farmer.2: The wild beasts turned savage this year. They used to flee from people.
dlg.farmer.3: They come from the north. Something in the forest drives them here.
dlg.farmer.4: My tools are in the chest. Take them; they are no use to me now.
dlg.farmer.5: Scatter three boars and I save the season. I ask no more.
dlg.farmer.6: My boy runs about here. Keep an eye out; I cannot watch him from the field.
dlg.fisher.1: Thank you. Word reached the village; two came this morning and saw the river.
dlg.fisher.10: Fish thinned, then vanished. The water grew heavy; it flows, but unwillingly.
dlg.fisher.11: I told the village; they laughed. A fisherman's tale, they said.
dlg.fisher.12: You go and tell them. They will believe you; they believe those who carry swords.
dlg.fisher.2: For years nobody believed me. It seems one must see to believe.
dlg.fisher.3: The library is on the north bank. Elan is there; he may talk to you.
dlg.fisher.4: I will set my nets again. In case the fish return.
dlg.fisher.5: And if they do not, I set them anyway. It is what I have done forty years.
dlg.fisher.6: Thank you, hero. On the river's behalf, thank you.
dlg.fisher.7: Welcome. I am Riva. Forty years I have fished this river.
dlg.fisher.8: This water used to run clear. You could count the stones below.
dlg.fisher.9: Three years ago something came down from the north. I have not seen the bottom since.
dlg.ghost.1: You took the crystal. The golem's chest is empty for the first time in a century.
dlg.ghost.10: Be careful. The one whose hands made him stands before you now.
dlg.ghost.2: I placed it there. I had hands in those days.
dlg.ghost.3: Now go west to the Desert Road. The oracle waits there.
dlg.ghost.4: Do not look behind you in the sand. It becomes a habit.
dlg.ghost.5: I shall remain here. I have nothing left to carry.
dlg.ghost.6: Stop, living one. No one has walked these ruins in a hundred years.
dlg.ghost.7: This was a temple. Now there is only a warden: the Stone Golem.
dlg.ghost.8: The crystal is in its chest. You cannot take it without breaking him.
dlg.ghost.9: He walks slowly but never tires. You will tire — reckon accordingly.
dlg.guard.1: Hold. Whoever passes this gate speaks to Old Aldric first.
dlg.guard.10: The wolves run in packs. A lone one comes to delay you.
dlg.guard.11: Sir Roland went that way; no word since. If you see him, bring word back.
dlg.guard.12: Be careful. I'll leave the gate open.
dlg.guard.2: That's my rule, not his order. Of three who entered the woods, two never returned.
dlg.guard.3: Aldric sits north of the square, under the big tree.
dlg.guard.4: I think he was expecting you. You match his description.
dlg.guard.5: Speak with him, then come back. I'll open the gate myself.
dlg.guard.6: Even if you're in a hurry — even then, speak to him first.
dlg.guard.7: You may pass. If you've spoken to Aldric, the rest is your affair.
dlg.guard.8: East lies the Dark Forest. The trees are thick and there is one path.
dlg.guard.9: It is dim even by day; judge distance by ear, not eye.
dlg.hermit.1: I live in seclusion. That does not mean I am alone.
dlg.hermit.2: Twenty years ago I lived in the village. Then I saw something.
dlg.hermit.3: I never told. Telling would make me mad; silence made me strange.
dlg.hermit.4: From here I watch the way of the world. A good spot; the view is clear.
dlg.hermit.5: What I saw is returning. This time everyone will see it.
dlg.hermit.6: You run. I sit. We are both waiting for the same thing.
dlg.inn.1: Welcome. The inn is empty, but the fire's lit and the bed is warm.
dlg.inn.2: Merchants used to stay the night; now nobody wants to be caught on the road.
dlg.inn.3: Eighteen gold a night. It mends both weariness and wounds.
dlg.inn.4: Whatever happens outside, I won't wake you. I promised that once.
dlg.inn.5: I sell potions too. Innkeeper by trade, but my first job is keeping people standing.
dlg.inn.6: Old Aldric comes weekly, drinks his tea, tells me nothing.
dlg.inn.7: If he's telling you, then things are truly bad.
dlg.kid.1: Are you a hero? Father said heroes were tall.
dlg.kid.2: Is your sword real? I won't touch it, I'm only asking.
dlg.kid.3: Last week I heard a sound from the forest. Father said wind. It wasn't.
dlg.kid.4: When I grow up I'll go there too. But first I'll learn to read.
dlg.kid.5: Will you tell me about it when you come back? I promise I'll stay awake.
dlg.king.1: So you did it. For a century I was a shadow waiting in this hall.
dlg.king.10: Let me tell you this: that crown speaks. Do not listen.
dlg.king.11: It told me I was right. It always tells you that you are right.
dlg.king.12: Be careful, hero. The last door is the easiest to open.
dlg.king.2: I sealed Malachar, and then remained inside the seal myself.
dlg.king.3: The crown had blackened. It darkens whoever bears it — it darkened me.
dlg.king.4: You did not put it on. That alone sets you apart from me.
dlg.king.5: The kingdom owes you, hero. Your name will enter the chronicles.
dlg.king.6: Now go. You need not watch this hall close.
dlg.king.7: Come no closer. I am Alderon — or what is left of him.
dlg.king.8: Malachar is strong. He is not to be beaten but bound.
dlg.king.9: Both crystals are needed. One opens the seal, the other closes it.
dlg.libr.1: All three are here! Forgive my shaking hands.
dlg.libr.10: They may lie in the ruins, the desert and the ice cave. If they walked, they walked there.
dlg.libr.11: Why there? Because the seal's four corners are there. The scrolls went home.
dlg.libr.12: Bring them and I pay well. Not for the coin — to read them.
dlg.libr.2: This library stood incomplete for forty years. Today it is whole.
dlg.libr.3: The scrolls describe Malachar's seal — how it was made, and how it fails.
dlg.libr.4: The seal is not a lock but a promise. Someone must repeat it each generation.
dlg.libr.5: No one did. It is nobody's fault; nobody knew.
dlg.libr.6: The chests are yours. Take them; I pay paper debts in gold.
dlg.libr.7: I am Elan, the librarian. Alone here these forty years.
dlg.libr.8: No fire, no theft. Three scrolls simply walked off one night.
dlg.oracle.1: You brought the second crystal. So you had the answer before the question.
dlg.oracle.11: Stop. Empty hands, full eyes. You are not ready yet.
dlg.oracle.12: Find the Earth Crystal first. It is in the ruins to the north-east.
dlg.oracle.13: I did not set the order. Four crystals are four doors, opened in turn.
dlg.oracle.14: Hurry and you will turn back. Turn back and you will come to me.
dlg.oracle.15: And I will say the same thing. Do not waste your time.
dlg.oracle.2: The Shadow Castle is open to you now. 'Open' is not always 'invited'.
dlg.oracle.3: A king is there. He thinks he is dead; he is wrong, which is worse.
dlg.oracle.4: Heed him, but not his crown. The crown is another thing's voice.
dlg.oracle.5: Go. I will not turn the glass again; that much is enough.
dlg.oracle.6: Welcome. I will not ask your name; the sand has it already.
dlg.oracle.7: You bear the Earth Crystal. The second lies at the bottom of the Ice Cave.
dlg.oracle.8: In the cave the cold will not kill you; stopping will. Keep walking.
dlg.oracle.9: A spirit dwells there; it will not lie, nor will it tell you all.
dlg.otaci.1: Ashveil's herbs were never this pale.
dlg.otaci.10: Take this mixture. It brings no sleep, but makes waking easier.
dlg.otaci.11: Keep this flask close. You never know the hour.
dlg.otaci.12: Come by if you return. If not, I shall assume you did.
dlg.otaci.2: I drew water from the northern spring; now it runs dark.
dlg.otaci.3: I can still brew, but each year it gets harder.
dlg.otaci.4: Take what you need, traveller. Your life is worth more than coin.
dlg.otaci.5: I gather and boil my own herbs. I trust no one else with it.
dlg.otaci.6: My prices are not high. You would pay if they were — I know that too.
dlg.otaci.7: They say you carry the crystals. Do your hands not shake yet?
dlg.otaci.8: The curse wears down the bearer, not just the soil.
dlg.otaci.9: Do you sleep at night? I ask because I can guess the answer.
dlg.roland.1: Well done. Judging by my wound, you moved faster than I did.
dlg.roland.10: I had never seen the like. There is a mind in this wood, and not a beast's.
dlg.roland.11: The Earth Crystal is in the ruins. Go north; I would only slow you.
dlg.roland.12: Beware: the Stone Golem guards it. Slow, but one blow is enough.
dlg.roland.2: The ruins lie north. The Stone Golem still guards the crystal in its chest.
dlg.roland.3: You cannot beat it without tiring it. Wait for its swing, then close.
dlg.roland.4: There is unexplored land south too; none have crossed past the meadows.
dlg.roland.5: I'll stay and hold this path. If my leg mends, I'll follow.
dlg.roland.6: If you reach the village, tell the guard I live.
dlg.roland.7: Ugh... keep back, my sword is still in hand. ...From the village? Good.
dlg.roland.8: I am Roland. I entered this forest three days ago; two days I cannot leave it.
dlg.roland.9: The wolves came in turns to wear me down. Not alone — in turns.
dlg.scout.1: If you came this far, you are not thinking of turning back.
dlg.scout.2: The pass is dangerous but passable. I have stood here ten years.
dlg.scout.3: South leads to the desert. Fill your water here; you'll find none there.
dlg.scout.4: East lie the ruins. I dislike them; the stones sit too neatly.
dlg.scout.5: Goblins come out from between the rocks. When hurt, they flee.
dlg.scout.6: Do not chase the runner. It draws you somewhere narrow, where it has friends.
dlg.scout.7: Be careful. I'll be here; if you return, we'll share a tea.
dlg.smith.1: Forty years at this forge, and never so few orders.
dlg.smith.2: Most who stayed ask for spades now, not swords.
dlg.smith.3: Still, iron is iron. Well-forged, it keeps you alive.
dlg.smith.4: Don't scorn what chests yield, but check it — rust tires the arm.
dlg.smith.5: Press [I] and open the Gear tab to see what you wear.
dlg.smith.6: If you have gold, we'll talk. If not, we'll still talk — but no iron.
dlg.smith.7: One more thing: they say Malachar's men carry no steel. If they did, I'd be afraid.
dlg.south.1: Head south and you'll see the meadows. Green as far as the eye goes.
dlg.south.2: I came from there; no wolves, no shadows. Only boars.
dlg.south.3: Find Farmer Torben in his field. A good man, and talkative.
dlg.south.4: His boy runs about there too; answer his questions or you'll hurt him.
dlg.south.5: I haul goods to the village; I'm off to the market now.
dlg.south.6: Stop by yourself. New stalls opened — not bad at all.
dlg.spirit.1: You took the crystal. The ice kept it a thousand years; you took a day.
dlg.spirit.10: Be careful. Ice makes no sound when it breaks.
dlg.spirit.2: The passage at the lower left opens to the Shadow Castle — only with a crystal.
dlg.spirit.3: There is no warmth there, and no sound. Grow used to both.
dlg.spirit.4: I am not the first to freeze in this cave, but I hope to be the last.
dlg.spirit.5: Walk on. If you stop, I stay with you — neither of us wants that.
dlg.spirit.6: Cold, is it not? After a while you stop noticing. That is the danger.
dlg.spirit.7: The crystal is in the deepest chamber, beyond the ice wolves.
dlg.spirit.8: The wolves come as a pack. Put your back to the ice and you need not watch it.
dlg.spirit.9: I cannot leave. But what I tell you leaves with you.
dlg.traveler.1: Fine meadows, are they not? Three days here, and no wish to leave.
dlg.traveler.2: A village north, a river west. Between them, only me.
dlg.traveler.3: I was a messenger once. Then every message I carried turned bad.
dlg.traveler.4: So I stopped. Now I only walk, carrying nothing to anyone.
dlg.traveler.5: You carry something, I think. Not your back — your face shows it.
dlg.traveler.6: Safe road. Sleep a night in this meadow; it will do no harm.
dlg.tuccar.1: I have crossed three kingdoms and seen nothing like this.
dlg.tuccar.10: Still, a good amulet is cheaper than a debt. Have a look.
dlg.tuccar.11: You need not be the fourth. Go prepared, that is all.
dlg.tuccar.12: If you return, I forgive your debt. I would like to carry one such.
dlg.tuccar.2: No caravans left on the roads; I come alone now.
dlg.tuccar.3: What I carry is light but precious: rings, amulets, sturdy boots.
dlg.tuccar.4: No haggling; the prices stand. That is the cost of the road.
dlg.tuccar.5: Ask and I'll tell: the best goods came with the northern caravans.
dlg.tuccar.6: They come no more. I'll sell what I have and leave the trade.
dlg.tuccar.7: You are bound for the Shadow Castle, aren't you? It shows in your eyes.
dlg.tuccar.8: I knew three who went. All three died owing me.
dlg.tuccar.9: Do not mistake me — the debt is nothing. I knew all three; that is the matter.
dlg.west.1: Going west? The river's there, and the bridge holds.
dlg.west.2: Riva the fisher lives on the bank. Mends nets all day, speaks to no one.
dlg.west.3: If he speaks, listen; he knows that river better than anyone.
dlg.west.4: They say an old library stands north of the river.
dlg.west.5: I've never seen it. Those who have said little.
dlg.west.6: Safe road. Return before dusk; in the dark the river's sound misleads.
dlg.witch.1: Welcome to the marsh. Nobody says that here; I do.
dlg.witch.2: They call me a witch. It is untrue, but I tired of correcting them.
dlg.witch.3: There is peace here, and danger. Both drink from the same water.
dlg.witch.4: Ancient powers sleep to the west. Do not wake them; they ask no one.
dlg.witch.5: Tread carefully. The marsh swallows the one who pauses, not the one who walks.
dlg.witch.6: Shall I give you something? I cannot. But I will tell you: do not drink the water.
dlg.witch.7: If you return to the village, do not mention me. My head aches when my name is said.
epi.1.1: Malachar's voice became a scream, then a whisper.
epi.1.2: Then it was nothing at all. The castle's stones fell silent for the first time.
epi.1.3: The Dark Crown fell and cracked under its own weight.
epi.1.4: You did not pick it up. That was the right choice.
epi.2.1: King Alderon's shade slowly came undone.
epi.2.2: "A hundred years I waited," he said. "Not to thank you —"
epi.2.3: "— but to see someone walk away without the crown."
epi.2.4: Then he too fell silent. The hall emptied and the doors opened.
epi.3.1: When you returned to Ashveil, Old Aldric was waiting at the gate.
epi.3.2: He asked nothing. He simply walked beside you.
epi.3.3: That night the village slept without lamps. First time in a century.
epi.3.4: The seal's promise is known now. Someone need only repeat it.
epi.boar.1: The meadow was harvested — whole for the first time in years.
epi.boar.2: Farmer Torben told his boy your name; the child did not believe him.
epi.fish.1: The West River ran clear again three days later.
epi.fish.2: Riva counted the stones on its bed and set his nets again.
epi.quiet.1: The marsh woman came down to the village. No one called her a witch.
epi.quiet.2: The hermit came down, stayed a night, returned at dawn. Enough, he said.
epi.scroll.1: Elan the librarian set the three scrolls on one shelf.
epi.scroll.2: He read the seal's promise aloud. This time someone was listening.
epi.title: The Dark Crown's End

story.11: One morning the sky darkens over Ashveil.
story.12: The seal weakens. Malachar is stirring...
story.14: The village elder calls for you.
story.15: Fate demands a hero once more.
story.2: The Shadow Lord MALACHAR spread his darkness
story.3: across the lands. Villages burned, peoples enslaved.
story.5: Four great heroes, with the crystals' power,
story.6: sealed Malachar in the Shadow Realm.

ui.sq_icewolf_desc: Scatter the ice wolves in the cave.
ui.sq_scorpion_desc: Clear the desert road of scorpions.
